subject: AcuteMed RFI: isolated deployment operator roles & connectivity details
body:
--- Message 1 ---
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acutemed.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acutemed.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capabilities follow-up: isolated deployment checklist (AcuteMed)

Hi Neha / Rafael,

Thanks for the high-level sheet last week. The procurement and cloud teams at AcuteMed have a couple of discrete asks so we can close the technical portion of the RFP: 

- A clear mapping of operator roles (who can start/stop runtime, who can access KV caches, who can push model updates) and how RBAC is enforced.
- Confirmation on KMS/HSM integration options. We run a customer-managed Vault cluster and need to understand whether Redwood can accommodate an HSM-backed key-encryption workflow for local secrets.
- Connectivity constraints for the on-prem control plane (what outbound endpoints are required, ports, IPs) and whether an air-gapped install is supported for acceptance testing.
- Example acceptance-test checklist for on-site operator handoff (we prefer stepwise runbook excerpts).

Can you respond with a statement of capabilities and any evidence artifacts (SOC2, attestation) you can share under NDA?

We'd like to schedule a short 30m sync this week if possible — Gabe from our cloud ops is available Wed/Thu mornings.

Appreciate it,
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Cloud Architecture
AcuteMed Health
[phone: +1 415 555 0147] 

--- Message 2 ---
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acutemed.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capabilities follow-up: isolated deployment checklist (AcuteMed)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below, followed by attachments with the expanded matrix and sample runbook excerpts. I'll also propose times for a sync.

1) Operator roles / RBAC
- Redwood Private supports role-based access controls (RBAC) mapped to operator personas: Ops-Admin, Runtime-Operator, Readonly-Audit, Model-Publisher.
- Authorization is backed by OAuth2 + SAML SSO for enterprise installs; for air-gapped/on-prem we support SAML over an IdP proxy or certificate-based operator identities.
- The attached operator_handoff_matrix.csv shows permitted actions per role (start/stop runtime, KV operations, model push, emergency rollback).

2) KMS / HSM
- Two modes supported: (A) Customer-managed KMS: Redwood can integrate with an on-prem Vault cluster using transit seal; keys never leave customer HSM/KMS. (B) HSM gateway: For strictly air-gapped sites we provide an HSM gateway adapter that performs encryption/decryption within the customer's FIPS 140-2 validated HSM appliance — we ship only signed connectors and a documented API.
- We will sign an NDA for deeper key management schematics.

3) Connectivity for control plane and air-gapped options
- Hosted control-plane mode requires outbound HTTPS to the control-hostnames listed in the attached PDF (AcuteMed_RFI_Response.pdf). For fully air-gapped installs we support a private control plane (customer-managed) and offer an on-prem control-plane appliance; acceptance tests run against local endpoints only.
- Baseline ports: 443 egress for telemetry when connected; for isolated acceptance testing only local ports are used — see section 3 in the PDF.

4) Acceptance test / operator handoff
- Attached is an excerpt runbook and a checklist used in prior on-site handoffs. Key items: operator account creation, RBAC verification, KV cache seeding and eviction test, model rollback simulation, patch-and-restart acceptance window.

Attachments included: AcuteMed_RFI_Response.pdf, operator_handoff_matrix.csv

Next steps:
- I'm available Wed 2 Jun 09:00–11:00 PT or Thu 3 Jun 09:00–12:00 PT for a 30m sync with your cloud ops team.
- If helpful, Rafael can provide a short note on the audit evidence we can share (SOC2 redacted, attestation process).

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
[Attachment: AcuteMed_RFI_Response.pdf (PDF, 87KB)]
[Attachment: operator_handoff_matrix.csv (CSV, 6KB)]

--- Message 3 ---
From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capabilities follow-up: isolated deployment checklist (AcuteMed)

Neha / Vanessa — adding a few implementation clarifications we should surface directly to Sarah/Gabe in the sync: 

- RBAC enforcement: runtime actions are mediated by an operator authorization layer in the control plane; we persist audit events locally and forward to customer SIEMs on demand. Role grants are stored in the customer-managed control-plane DB for private deployments so revocations are immediate (no cloud round-trip required).
- KV caching: operator roles can be restricted at keyspace level; we support namespaces and per-model policy bindings.
- HSM gateway specifics: the adapter runs in a segregated process namespace and communicates with the HSM over the vendor-specified channel (PKCS#11 or vendor API). For evidence, we can provide a redacted integration diagram and a hardened connector checksum list.

I'll join the call if it's scheduled during my window.

-Rafael
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-report-redacted.pdf (PDF, redacted, 120KB)]

--- Message 4 ---
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acutemed.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Gabe Morales <gabe@cloudops-svc.com>, procurement@acutemed.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capabilities follow-up: isolated deployment checklist (AcuteMed)

Thanks — this is helpful. Two quick follow-ups: 

1) Can you add a maintenance_escalation_matrix.xlsx showing who is contacted for P1/P2 incidents during onboarding and after cutover? We need explicit SLA contact points.
2) We require an in-scope SOC2 (redacted is fine) plus a simple attestation letter confirming no persistent customer data leaves our network in private mode. Can you confirm and, if possible, provide a short templated attestation we can include in our procurement packet?

Gabe: are Wed/Thu AM still OK?

Best,
Sarah

--- Message 5 ---
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acutemed.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capabilities follow-up: isolated deployment checklist (AcuteMed)

Sarah / Gabe / procurement team —

Attached is the maintenance_escalation_matrix.xlsx (stub) and our redacted SOC2. Short answer to your attestation request: yes — for Redwood Private deployed in customer-managed (on-prem/VPC) mode, we provide an attestation that no persistent customer data is transmitted to Redwood-hosted systems. Transient telemetry (optionally enabled) can be configured to use customer-managed endpoints; details and opt-in configuration are in section 4 of the PDF.

I attached a one-page attestation template as well (see the PDF, page 2). If that passes your legal, we can add it to the procurement packet and circulate a DocuSign link for a mutual confidentiality addendum before sharing any unredacted artifacts.

Proposed short call times: Wed 3 Jun 10:00 PT or Thu 4 Jun 09:30 PT. Please confirm.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
